text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 6: Training gain describes splits; feature tests decide usefulness'
text.tspan: Figure 6: Training gain describes splits; feature tests decide

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Corrected wind and radiation inputs; squared-error models fitted separately for each meter using all 24 production features. Training periods: April 2024 to June 2025 and July 2025 to June 2026. Each meter's model is fitted three times for each training period, using different random seeds: six refits per meter. Blue dot: mean gain share. Blue line: minimum to maximum across the six refits. Each model's feature gains are scaled to sum to one; unused columns receive zero. Meters of one type have equal weight within each refit; the six refits have equal weight. Ranges describe variability across refits, not confidence intervals. Horizontal axes are logarithmic, with a display floor of 0.01% of training gain. Means and range endpoints below the floor, including zero, are displayed at the floor. A mark at the floor does not establish positive gain; reported shares remain unchanged. Gain divides credit between correlated features and does not establish benefit.'
text.tspan: Corrected wind and radiation inputs; squared-error models fitted separately for each meter using all 24 production
Training periods: April 2024 to June 2025 and July 2025 to June 2026.
Each meter's model is fitted three times for each training period, using different random seeds: six refits per
Blue dot: mean gain share. Blue line: minimum to maximum across the six refits.
Each model's feature gains are scaled to sum to one; unused columns receive zero.
Meters of one type have equal weight within each refit; the six refits have equal weight.
Ranges describe variability across refits, not confidence intervals.
Horizontal axes are logarithmic, with a display floor of 0.01% of training gain.
Means and range endpoints below the floor, including zero, are displayed at the floor.
A mark at the floor does not establish positive gain; reported shares remain unchanged.
Gain divides credit between correlated features and does not establish benefit.
